when: one enemy is dead and all five of your team are alive
asks: we're five v four what do we do
one of them is dead, now what
they're down a guy, do we fight
numbers advantage, what do we take
say: You're five against four, so force the nearest tower or objective now, or just shove waves if their respawn is under ten seconds.
more: A numbers edge is only worth what you take with it. If nothing falls before the respawn, the kill was just a little gold.
Pick the closest thing. Walking across the map to a better prize usually spends the whole death timer.
A tower taken now also opens the approach to the next dragon or Baron, so it pays again a few minutes later.
check: How long is the respawn timer, and what is actually within a short walk of your team?
breaks: Wrong if your team is low or scattered across three lanes: shove the wave you're in and recall on the gold instead.
basis: pro:After a won fight, the waves decide whether you got paid

when: one ally is dead and all five enemies are alive
asks: we're down one, do we fight
four v five, should we go
our guy just died, what now
can we still take this fight
say: You're a player down, so back off and clear waves from range, or give this one up and take camps on the far side.
more: Four against five loses most even fights. The team with the extra body gets a free angle on your carry.
Giving ground for one death timer is cheap. Losing two more players turns a small loss into a tower or an objective.
If they start something, look for what is open elsewhere right then, not after they finish.
check: Who died, how long is their timer, and are the enemies grouped or spread out?
breaks: Wrong if the dead ally matters little to fights and the enemies are low or split: then a fight at your tower can still be good.
basis: pro:Arrive together or do not arrive

when: one player on each team is dead
asks: it's four v four, do we fight
we both lost one, who's ahead
traded one each, keep going?
four on four, is that good for us
say: Fight on if their dead player is the bigger carry, or back up and wait if it's your damage that's missing.
more: Equal numbers are not equal fights. Compare items and levels of the two dead players, then of the eight still standing.
Losing a support or tank hurts less in a short skirmish than losing the one player who deals the damage.
Also compare timers. Whoever respawns first gets a short five against four at the end of it.
check: Which of the two dead players has more items, and whose respawn timer is shorter?
breaks: Wrong if the survivors on your side are low on health: numbers and items don't help a team that dies to the first ability.

when: two or more enemies are dead after 20:00
asks: two of them are dead, baron?
we got two kills, what do we take
double kill, do we go baron
they're down two, what now
say: Two down is enough for Baron if their jungler is one of them, or take the nearest tower if he's still alive.
more: Baron is slow, and a living enemy jungler turns it into a Smite contest you don't need to take.
With their jungler dead there is no reliable last hit, so three defenders usually stay home and clear waves.
A tower is the safe payment. It cannot be stolen and it brings your waves closer to their base for the next push.
check: Is their jungler one of the dead, how long are the timers, and how healthy is your team?
breaks: Wrong if your team is far from the top pit or low on health: take the tower in front of you and reset instead.
basis: pro:A dead jungler makes the objective free

when: your jungler is dead and a dragon or Baron is up
asks: our jungler's dead, do we contest
no smite, can we still fight for it
jungler died before dragon, what now
should we give this objective
say: No Smite on your side, so don't contest it; push a side tower instead, or hold mid and clear if nothing's reachable.
more: Without your jungler the last hit is a coin flip weighted against you, and you fight a player short as well.
The answer is to be paid somewhere else at the same moment they commit, while their bodies are in the pit.
Start the trade when they start. If you wait to see how it goes, they finish and still arrive to defend.
check: How long is your jungler's timer, and which enemy tower or camp can you reach before they finish?
breaks: Wrong if this is their soul dragon or Elder: then stall at range with wave clear and poke until your jungler is back.
basis: pro:If you cannot contest, take something elsewhere at once

when: the enemy jungler is dead
asks: their jungler's dead, do I leave lane
enemy jungle died, should I help
do I go to dragon or stay
jungler's down, what's my job
say: Their Smite is gone, so leave your wave and help start the objective, or shove first if your jungler isn't there yet.
more: This is the safest objective you get all game. The only thing that can spoil it is not having enough damage to finish in time.
A laner arriving turns a slow solo take into a fast one, which is what beats the respawn timer.
A few lost minions are a small price. The objective stays on the scoreboard and the minions come back.
check: Is an objective actually up, where is your jungler, and how long is the enemy jungler's timer?
breaks: Wrong if nothing is up or your jungler is on the other side: use the window to shove and take plates or a tower instead.
basis: pro:A dead jungler makes the objective free

when: your team's most-itemed carry is dead
asks: our carry's dead, can we fight
adc died, do we still go
we lost our damage, now what
fed guy's dead, what do we do
say: Your main damage is down, so don't take a fight; clear waves under tower, or trade a far tower if they commit to an objective.
more: Four players without the damage dealer can start a fight but usually cannot finish one.
Their team knows it too and will try to force something now. The job is to give them as little as possible for one timer.
When your carry is back, the fight you refused is still available, on your terms.
check: How long is the carry's timer, and what are the enemies walking toward?
breaks: Wrong if their carry is dead too, or if another teammate is nearly as strong: then judge it as an even fight.

when: an ally's respawn timer is under ten seconds
asks: should we wait for him to respawn
he's almost back, do we fight now
wait or go
do we hold for our last guy
say: Hold a few seconds until your teammate is back and walking up, or fight now if they've started the objective and it's low.
more: A few seconds of patience turns four against five into an even fight. Starting early throws that away.
Remember the walk. Respawning is not arriving, so stall near your side of the fight rather than in the middle.
Use the wait to shove a wave or drop a ward, so the fight starts with something already in your favour.
check: How far is the fight from your base, and how low is the objective they are hitting?
breaks: Wrong if they're about to finish Baron, soul or Elder: then someone has to contest immediately, even short-handed.
basis: pro:Arrive together or do not arrive

when: the dead enemies' respawn timers are under ten seconds
asks: they're about to respawn, do we stay
should we keep hitting the tower
do we back off now
how long can we stay here
say: Their timers are almost up, so bank what you've got and leave now, or stay only if the tower dies in a few more hits.
more: The window closes when they respawn near their base, fresh, with you low and deep in their side.
Most thrown leads come from staying for one more thing. Leaving on time keeps the gold and lets you spend it.
A clean recall now means you return with items before they can set up the next objective.
check: How much health does the tower have, and how healthy is your team?
breaks: Wrong if the tower or inhibitor is nearly dead and your wave is big: finish it, then leave together through one path.
basis: pro:When ahead, let them come to you

when: you are dead
asks: I'm dead, what should my team do
what do I do when I respawn
I just died, now what
dead again, what's the plan
say: While you're dead, ping your team back; when you're up, walk out with the next wave, or buy and defend if they're pushing.
more: Your death timer is their window. The best help you can give is stopping teammates from fighting without you.
Use the time to plan the purchase, so you spend the moment you are alive and lose no seconds in the shop.
Walking out with a wave gives you cover and something to push. Running out alone to rejoin is how the second death happens.
check: How long is your timer, how much gold do you have, and which objective spawns next?
breaks: Wrong if your team is already in a winning fight nearby: then come straight in from a safe side rather than waiting for a wave.

when: after 30:00
asks: what's the plan this late
how do we win from here
it's late game, what matters now
what should we be doing right now
say: Death timers are long now, so one pick can decide Baron or the game; stay grouped, or sidelane only with teammates close by.
more: Late on, a single death can cost a Baron, an Elder or the base, because the team plays a player short for a long time.
That cuts both ways. Catching one of them alone is worth far more than any amount of farm.
So the plan is simple: push waves safely, hold vision around the next big objective, and never be the one found alone.
check: Which big objective is up next, and where are the side waves?
breaks: Wrong if you're far behind and grouped fights are hopeless: then careful side pressure with an escape is the better hope.

when: numbers are even and your team is behind in levels and items
asks: it's five v five, can we fight
we're behind, do we take this fight
should we fight even numbers
they're stronger, what do we do
say: Even numbers don't make it an even fight; make them come through your tower, or pick off whoever walks up alone.
more: Levels and finished items decide a straight five on five more than who starts it.
A tower, a narrow approach or a wave of your minions can cover part of that gap, so choose where the fight happens.
Catching one player first changes the count, and a numbers edge is the one thing that beats an item edge.
check: How big is the item gap on the carries, and is there a tower or wave nearby to fight beside?
breaks: Wrong if they are sieging with Baron buff or taking soul: then waiting loses anyway, and you need the best engage you can find.
basis: pro:Do not fight an objective one spike behind

when: before 14:00
asks: there's a fight in river, do I go
should I leave lane to help
skirmish in river, join or stay
jungler's fighting, do I rotate
say: Count who gets there first: join if your lane shoved and you're healthy, or stay and take the minions if you'd arrive second.
more: Early river fights are won by the second and third body, not by the two junglers.
Arriving late is the worst result. You lose the wave and walk into a fight that's already decided.
Staying is not doing nothing. The minions and plates you take are the payment if the fight goes badly.
check: Is your wave pushed, is your opponent already moving, and how much health do you have?
breaks: Wrong if your opponent has left first with their wave shoved in: ping it, follow only if you can catch up, otherwise push hard.
basis: pro:Count who can actually arrive before contesting

when: all five enemies are dead before 20:00
asks: we aced them, what do we take
ace, now what
they're all dead, what do we do
everybody's dead, towers or dragon
say: They're all dead, so take the closest tower, then dragon or Herald, or go straight to the objective if the tower's too healthy.
more: Timers are short this early, so you get one thing for certain and a second only if it is close by.
A tower is permanent and opens the map. A dragon builds toward soul. Either beats five people chasing nothing.
Decide in the first seconds. An ace wasted on arguing about where to go is the common way to get nothing.
check: Which tower is closest and how healthy is it, and is a dragon or Herald up?
breaks: Wrong if your survivors are very low: one healthy respawn can clean up, so shove the wave and recall instead.
basis: pro:After a won fight, the waves decide whether you got paid

when: all five enemies are dead after 25:00
asks: we aced them, can we end
ace, do we end or baron
all dead, go for the win?
can we finish the game now
say: Push mid together and end if minions are with you and their timers outlast the walk, or take Baron and an inhibitor instead.
more: Ending needs three things: enough of you alive, a wave to tank the towers, and timers longer than the walk plus the hitting.
If any one is missing, Baron plus an inhibitor makes the next push close to certain.
The mistake is doing half of each: walking to their base, getting stopped, and having no time left for Baron.
check: How many of you are alive, where is the nearest wave, and how long is the shortest enemy timer?
breaks: Wrong if their inhibitor towers are still up and no wave is close: you will not get through in time, so take Baron.

when: all five enemies are dead and only one or two of your team are alive
asks: we aced but it's just me left
only two of us alive, what do we take
I'm the last one standing, now what
we won but everyone's dead
say: With so few of you left, take the nearest tower with a wave, or recall and spend the gold if no wave's there.
more: One or two players kill objectives slowly, and a big monster can kill you when you're already low.
A tower with minions tanking is the safe prize. Without minions the tower just hits you.
If nothing is safe, the fight still paid: you have the gold and they do not, so turn it into items first.
check: How much health do you have, and is there a friendly wave near any enemy tower?
breaks: Wrong if you're healthy, their timers are long and a dragon is right there: a careful dragon is fine.

when: your whole team is dead
asks: we got aced, what now
everyone's dead, what do we do
we just lost that fight, now what
how do we come back from that
say: You'll lose something here; when you respawn, defend the base together, or clear the biggest wave first if they went to Baron.
more: After an ace the choice is theirs. Your choice is what to protect first when you are back.
Respawns are staggered. The first one alive should clear waves from safety, not walk out to meet five people.
If they took Baron, the next minutes are about wave clear in every lane and refusing fights until the buff ends.
check: Who respawns first, what are they hitting, and how much gold can you spend right now?
breaks: Wrong if they are low and still in your base as several of you respawn together: then a fight at your own towers can turn it.

when: the enemy support is dead and a dragon or Baron spawns within a minute
asks: we killed their support, what now
support's dead, do we set up
got a pick on support, dragon?
their support's down, what do we do
say: Their vision player is down, so ward the pit and set up now, or start it immediately if it's already up.
more: Supports carry most of a team's wards and sweeping. Without theirs, the river goes dark for them.
A team that walks in blind has to guess where you are, and that is when picks and good engages happen.
Arriving early and holding vision is worth more than the extra kill you might get by chasing the other four.
check: Do you and your support have wards and a sweeper, and how long until the spawn?
breaks: Wrong if the support respawns well before the objective does: then just take the vision and a wave, not a fight.
basis: pro:Before a spawn, arrive alive and on time

when: the enemy's most-itemed carry is dead after 20:00
asks: we killed their carry, baron?
their adc's dead, what do we do
got the fed guy, now what
carry's down, do we go
say: Their damage is gone, so start Baron right away, or siege the nearest tower if their jungler's healthy and you lack damage.
more: Without their carry they cannot win a fight in the pit, so the only threat left is a Smite steal.
Zone their jungler away from the pit rather than racing him. One player on him is usually enough.
If Baron would be slow, a tower is the safer payment, and it still makes the next Baron easier to hold.
check: How long is the carry's timer, where is their jungler, and how fast can your team kill Baron?
breaks: Wrong if your own team is low or your jungler is dead: take a tower and recall, the pick already gave you tempo.
basis: pro:If you cannot win the Smite duel, remove their jungler

when: one enemy is dead between 14:00 and 20:00
asks: we got a pick, baron's not up, what now
one dead, what do we take
killed one, where do we go
pick, dragon or tower
say: Baron isn't up yet, so turn the pick into dragon or an outer tower, or Herald if you're already top side.
more: Before twenty minutes the top pit holds Herald, not Baron, so the prizes are smaller and timers are short.
That makes distance the deciding factor. Take whichever is nearest to where the kill happened.
An outer tower near the next dragon is a good default. It makes the following spawn easier to control.
check: Where did the kill happen, is a dragon up, and has Herald already been taken?
breaks: Wrong if the grubs or Herald were already taken and the dragon is down: then it is towers and deep wards only.

when: one enemy is dead and no dragon or Baron is up
asks: we got a kill but nothing's up
pick but no objective, what now
killed one, nothing to take
what do we do with this kill
say: Nothing big is up, so shove that lane and take their nearby camps, or recall on the gold if a spawn's coming.
more: A kill with no objective still buys time. Spend it on things that set up the next spawn.
A shoved wave and stolen camps cost them gold and force someone to come and clear.
A recall timed off a kill is free: you come back with items while they are still walking out.
check: Which objective spawns next and when, and how much gold are you holding?
breaks: Wrong if the rest of their team is grouped nearby: take the wave only, and stay out of their jungle.
basis: pro:A trade needs something real to take

when: one ally and one enemy died in the last 20 seconds
asks: we traded one for one, keep fighting?
one for one, is that good
we both lost a guy, do we go again
even trade, now what
say: A one-for-one changes little by itself; back off and reset, or press on only if your survivors are healthier and closer to the objective.
more: After an even trade, the fight belongs to whichever side still has health, ultimates and position.
Check what each kill was worth. Trading your support for their carry is a win, the reverse is not.
If it is unclear, resetting costs nothing. A second fight started on low health usually goes to the team that waited.
check: Who has more health left, and which two players died?
breaks: Wrong if the objective is one hit from dead and your jungler is alive: finish it first, then leave.

when: your team got two or more kills in the last 20 seconds
asks: do we chase them
should we keep chasing
they're running, do we follow
we won the fight, now what
say: Stop chasing once they reach their tower; send one player to the side wave and take a structure, or the objective if it's up.
more: The fight is won when they run. What matters next is what the map pays you for it.
If all five chase, the survivors escape anyway and the dead respawn onto waves pushed into your towers.
One player catching the side wave keeps your lanes healthy, so the next push starts from a good position.
check: Where are the side waves, and how long are the death timers?
breaks: Wrong if a low enemy carry is in the open with no escape and nothing blocks you: one more kill there can end it.
basis: pro:After a won fight, the waves decide whether you got paid

asks: he's one hit, do I chase
should I follow him into the jungle
he's low, can I go get him
do I chase this kill
say: Let him go if you'd lose sight of him in their jungle, or follow only with two teammates and vision ahead.
more: A low enemy running into darkness is running toward his team. The kill is small and your death is large.
Chasing also leaves the wave or objective you were winning. That is often the bigger loss.
If you do follow, go as a group and stop at the first brush you cannot see into.
check: Can you see where he is heading, and where are his teammates on the map?
breaks: Wrong if he has no escape, his team shows on the other side of the map and you're healthy: then finish him.
basis: pro:When ahead, let them come to you

asks: should I keep hitting their tank
the tank's running, do we chase
their front line's low, follow?
do we kill the tank
say: A tank running away is usually bait; turn back to the wave or objective, or keep going only if their carries are dead.
more: Tanks take a long time to kill, and every second spent on one pulls your team toward their damage.
The moment your front line is deep, their carries hit freely and the fight flips.
If their carries are already dead, the tank has nobody to turn with, and then finishing him is fine.
check: Are their damage dealers alive and nearby, and how far have you been pulled from your own carry?
breaks: Wrong if the tank is truly isolated and nearly dead: a fast kill on him still opens the next objective.

asks: do I chase as adc
they're running, do I follow
should I walk up and finish them
can I go in for the kill
say: Hit whoever's in range and let your front line do the chasing, or walk forward only once their divers are dead.
more: Your damage wins the fight, so the only way to lose a won fight is for you to die chasing.
A carry walking past their own front line is what every assassin waits for.
Staying on the nearest target keeps your damage constant, and the kills come to you as they try to turn.
check: Which enemy divers are still alive, and is anyone on your team still next to you?
breaks: Wrong if everyone who can jump on you is dead: then walk up and take everything you can reach.

when: three enemies are dead and two are alive after 25:00
asks: three dead, can we end
two left, do we dive the base
do we chase the last two
end or baron
say: Two defenders with wave clear can hold a base, so take Baron then inhibitors, or end only if minions are already on their nexus towers.
more: Two players under towers and at their fountain are much stronger than two players in the open.
Baron with three of them dead is close to free, and it makes the base fall on the next push.
Ending is right when the wave is already there. Without minions the towers will buy them the time to respawn.
check: Where is your wave, how long are the three timers, and do the two survivors clear waves well?
breaks: Wrong if Baron was just taken and is not up: then take the inhibitor the wave is closest to and reset.

asks: where should we fight
do we fight in the jungle or in lane
where's a good spot for my ult
where do I want this fight
say: Your area damage is strongest where they're squeezed together, so fight in jungle paths or the pit, or poke first if they're spread in lane.
more: Narrow paths force five players into one ability. In an open lane the same ability hits one or two.
So let them walk to you through the jungle and hold the big ability for that moment.
This is also why objectives suit you. A team hitting a monster is standing in a small space.
check: Which path will they come through, and is it warded so you see them before they see you?
breaks: Wrong if their team has more area damage than yours: then the choke hurts you more, and open ground is safer.
basis: pro:Who starts the objective depends on who wants to be pinned

asks: where should I stand in fights
where do we want to fight
should we fight in the river
is this a good place to fight
say: Take fights in a lane or open river where you can kite back, or skip it if the only way in is a narrow path.
more: Room to walk backward while attacking is what keeps you alive. Walls take that away.
In a narrow path one ability hits your whole team, and their divers reach you in a step.
If the fight has to be in the jungle, let your front line go first and stay a screen behind it.
check: Is there open space behind you, and which of their champions can jump onto you?
breaks: Wrong if the objective is being taken and it matters, like soul or Baron: then go in behind your tank rather than give it.

when: the enemy team has a champion with a large area engage
asks: how do we fight their engage
they have a big ult, where do we stand
how do we not get wombo'd
what do we do about their engage
say: Don't walk through narrow jungle in a clump; spread out and come in through lane, or give the objective if there's no safe way.
more: A big area engage needs you bunched and close. Spacing takes most of its value away.
Once it has been used, even on one player, the next stretch is your time to fight or start an objective.
So approach slowly, let them show it, and only then commit.
check: Did you see the engage ability or Flash used recently, and which path keeps your team spread?
breaks: Wrong if that champion is dead or just used the ultimate: then group and take the fight straight away.
basis: pro:Cooldowns spent before the objective decide it

asks: we're a poke comp, how do we fight
should we just engage
do we fight or poke
how do we win fights with poke
say: Stay at range and wear them down before anything starts, or back off completely if their engage gets within reach of you.
more: Your team wins the fight before it begins. A team at half health cannot contest an objective.
Arrive first, and make them walk into your abilities to reach the pit or tower.
Do not start the objective yourselves while they're healthy. Hitting it pins you in a small space for their engage.
check: How healthy are they after the poke, and where is their main engager standing?
breaks: Wrong if they are already low across the board: then stop poking and take the objective or the tower.
basis: pro:Who starts the objective depends on who wants to be pinned

asks: we're a dive comp, how do we fight
who do we go on
do we all go in
how do we fight their front line
say: Go in together on one back-line target at the same moment, or wait for them to use their key crowd control first.
more: A dive works when several of you land at once. One at a time, each diver gets stopped and killed in turn.
Their front line is not your problem. Go past it, and the tanks are left with nobody to protect.
Patience helps. If the ability that stops you has been used, the same dive becomes much safer.
check: Which of their abilities stops a dive, and have you seen it used?
breaks: Wrong if you're behind and their carry has several protectors: split their attention with a side lane instead of diving.

when: the enemy team has assassins or divers
asks: they keep diving our carry, what do we do
how do we fight a dive comp
they jump our backline every time
how do we protect our adc
say: Stand close to your carry and kill whoever jumps in first, or step up to their front line only when their divers are down.
more: Against a dive, the fight happens around your carry. Meet them there instead of fighting their tanks far forward.
The first diver in takes everyone's crowd control and usually dies. That is the fight won.
Do not use everything on their engage tank. Keep stuns and shields for the player who goes for your carry.
check: Which enemy is the main diver, and is he alive and missing from view?
breaks: Wrong if their divers are behind and your front line can simply run them over: then fight forward as normal.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as tank
when do I engage
should I go in
do I start the fight
say: You start it: go when your carries are close enough to follow, or stand in front and soak if they're not in range.
more: An engage with nobody behind it is a death. Look at where your damage is before you look at the enemy.
If no good engage exists, being a wall between their team and your carry is still a full job.
The best moment is when they step up for a wave or an objective and are briefly bunched.
check: Are your damage dealers within range to follow, and is your engage ability up?
breaks: Wrong if your team is a player down or far behind: hold the engage to stop theirs instead.

asks: what do I do in fights as an assassin
when do I go in
who do I kill
do I go for the adc
say: Stay out of sight until their crowd control is used, then go for the carry, or kill the support first if the carry's protected.
more: Showing early tells them where to hold their stun. Showing late means it is already gone.
Any squishy kill at the start makes it five against four. It does not have to be the best target.
After the kill, get out. An assassin who stays to fight the tanks gives the kill back.
check: Which of their abilities stops you, and who is standing furthest from their team?
breaks: Wrong if you're behind on items and cannot kill a carry quickly: then guard your own carry and kill what dives.

asks: who do I hit as adc
what do I do in teamfights
do I hit the tank
should I go for their carry
say: Hit the closest target you can safely reach, even a tank, or back out and come in again if a diver's on you.
more: Steady damage on whoever is in front of you wins long fights. Walking past tanks to reach a carry loses them.
Stepping back for a moment is not giving up. A dead carry deals nothing, a patient one deals damage all fight.
Their front line dying first is normal. After that the back line has nothing between it and you.
check: Who can jump on you, and where are your tank and support standing?
breaks: Wrong if their carry walks into your range with nothing between you: then take the free shots on them.

asks: what do I do in fights as support
who do I shield
where do I stand as enchanter
who do I stay with
say: Stay behind your strongest carry and keep everything for whoever's being dived, or shield your engager if nobody's threatening the back.
more: Your abilities are worth the most on the player dealing the damage. Look at items and kills to decide who that is.
You are also an easy kill. Standing behind the carry means divers must pass through your team to reach you.
If the fight is going forward and nobody is diving, put the shields on whoever is in front.
check: Which teammate has the most items, and which enemy is trying to reach them?
breaks: Wrong if your carry is dead: switch to keeping the next strongest player alive, or help everyone disengage.

asks: what do I do in fights as a bruiser
do I dive their backline
front line or flank
who do I go on
say: Walk at their carries and make them use everything on you, or turn and peel your own carry if you're the one behind.
more: You are both a threat and a wall. Which one you play depends on whether you are stronger than their carries.
Ahead, they must deal with you first, and that buys your team the whole fight.
Behind, you die before you reach anyone, so stay back and hit whoever comes to you.
check: How do your level and items compare with their carries?
breaks: Wrong if their team kites well and you have no way to close the gap: wait for an engage from someone else.

asks: what do I do in fights as a mage
where do I put my abilities
do I save my ult
who do I hit
say: Put your zone where they have to walk and hit the front line safely, or hold your big ability for whoever dives you.
more: Your job is to make an area of the fight unwalkable. That splits their team more reliably than any single kill.
Like a marksman, you deal steady damage to what is in reach. Do not step forward for a perfect cast.
Holding one ability for self-defence is not wasteful when their assassin is alive and unseen.
check: Where will they walk to reach your team, and is their assassin or diver showing?
breaks: Wrong if they are already clumped at the start: then use the big ability immediately rather than saving it.

asks: what's my job in fights as support
do I engage or peel
should I go in
do I hook or stay back
say: Look for the engage on whoever steps up, or stay beside your carry and peel if their divers are ahead.
more: Decide before the fight which job matters more: starting it or protecting. Trying to do both does neither.
If their divers are stronger than your carry can handle alone, your crowd control belongs on them.
If your team is the stronger one, a catch on anyone, even a tank out of position, is a fine start.
check: Is your team ahead or behind, and who on their side is a threat to your carry?
breaks: Wrong if your carry is not in range to follow: an engage then just gives them a free kill on you.

asks: when do I go in as a duelist
do I go first
what do I do in teamfights
should I wait
say: Come in second, after the first crowd control lands, and clean up, or take the flank if the front is too crowded.
more: Skirmishers do well in a messy fight and badly as the first target, so let someone else take the opening abilities.
A flank gives you a short road to their carries, and makes them turn away from your team.
Leave when you are low and come back when your abilities are up. Staying alive keeps the pressure on.
check: Has their main crowd control been used, and can you reach the flank without being seen?
breaks: Wrong if nobody on your team can start the fight: then you have to wait for them to come to you.

asks: should I group or split
do I join the fight
team wants me to group, do I
stay side or come mid
say: Stay in the side lane and pull one or two over while your team stalls, or join if your Teleport's up and a fight starts.
more: Your pressure only works while your team refuses to fight four against five. Tell them that with pings.
If two come for you, your team has numbers at the objective. If nobody comes, you take the tower.
Teleport is what lets you do both. Without it, be on the same side of the map as the next objective.
check: Is your Teleport up, how many enemies are showing elsewhere, and which objective is next?
breaks: Wrong if your team keeps fighting without you and losing: group for the next objective rather than winning a lane alone.
basis: pro:Teleport decides who has the extra player

asks: I'm the carry, how do I fight
what do I do late game as carry
how do I not die in fights
when do I go in
say: You're the win condition now, so enter last and from behind your tank, or skip the fight if your protectors are dead.
more: Late on, your team's damage is mostly you. A fight where you die first is lost whatever else happens.
Arriving a moment late costs little. The key abilities are used on someone else, and then you hit freely.
If your tank and support are down, there is no front line to stand behind, and waiting for them is the better play.
check: Are your tank and support alive, and which enemy abilities are meant for you?
breaks: Wrong if they are taking Elder or your base: then you have to fight now, as safely as you can manage.

asks: who do I focus
who should I hit
which one do I attack
who's the target
say: Hit the carry only if you can reach them without dying; otherwise kill whoever's closest, or peel if your own carry's in trouble.
more: The best target is the one you can keep hitting. Damage on a tank still counts, damage you never deal does not.
If you are ranged, that means nearest first. If you dive, that means their weakest back-line player.
Check your own carry between abilities. Saving them is often worth more than the kill you were chasing.
check: Who is in your range right now, and is anyone on your carry?
breaks: Wrong if one enemy is far ahead and reachable: killing him first matters more than the usual order.

when: you have the most kills and items on your team
asks: I'm fed, how do I teamfight
I'm ahead, do I go in first
how do I carry this fight
I'm strong, what do I do
say: You're the threat, so don't go first; let someone else start, then finish it, or split a side lane to draw two of them.
more: They will hold every stun for you. If someone else starts, those abilities get used before you arrive.
Dying first with the lead is the comeback they are hoping for. It gives away the bounty as well as the fight.
In a side lane you force them to send two, and your team gets a numbers edge at the objective.
check: Which of their abilities are being saved for you, and is anyone else able to start the fight?
breaks: Wrong if nobody else on your team can engage and they are sieging: then you start it, on the most isolated target.
basis: pro:When ahead, let them come to you

when: you are behind in level and items
asks: I'm behind, what do I do in fights
I'm useless, how do I help
I do no damage, what's my job
how do I fight from behind
say: You won't win on damage, so land your crowd control on their carry and get out, or guard your own carry instead.
more: A player who is behind still has abilities that slow, stun or block. Those do not need items.
Stand where you are not the first target. Dying at the start makes it four against five for no return.
Guarding your strongest teammate is a real contribution. Their damage is your team's damage.
check: Which teammate is strongest, and what crowd control or utility do you have?
breaks: Wrong if their carries are just as far behind as you: then fight normally.

asks: should I flank
do I go around
flank or stay with team
can I come from behind
say: Flank only through a side they can't see and arrive as the fight starts, or walk in with your team if you'd be spotted.
more: A flank works on surprise and timing. Early, you are alone against five. Late, the fight is over.
A flanker who is seen has just split his own team, and the enemy turns on the smaller half.
Sweep or ward the path first. One enemy ward there makes the whole plan worthless.
check: Is the flank path dark for them, and can your team survive until you arrive?
breaks: Wrong if your team needs you in front to protect the carry: then the flank costs more than it gains.

when: you are level 6 and the enemy opposite you is level 5
asks: I just hit six, do I fight
I'm six and he's five, go?
should I fight now
I have my ult, do I use it
say: You have an ultimate and they don't, so take the skirmish now, or shove and recall if their jungler's level 6 as well.
more: A level is stats and, at six, a whole extra ability. That edge is short, because they catch up within a wave or two.
Used well it becomes a kill, a burned Flash or control of the next objective.
If their jungler already has his ultimate, the trade can turn, so a clean shove and recall is the safer payment.
check: How close is your opponent to level 6, and where was their jungler last seen?
breaks: Wrong if you are low on health or mana: then the level only makes the trade even, and it is better to reset.
basis: pro:Early on, a level is worth more than a little gold

when: your team killed Baron in the last minute
asks: we got baron, now what
how do we use baron
baron buff, where do we go
what do we do with baron
say: Recall, buy, then push three lanes with buffed waves at once, or go as five down one lane if they out-duel you in the sides.
more: The buff makes minions near you much harder to clear, so its value is towers, not fights.
Three lanes pushing at once is more than a team can answer. Something falls wherever they do not send people.
Grouping as five is slower but safer when their side laners would beat yours one on one.
check: Where are the three waves, and who on your team can safely hold a side lane?
breaks: Wrong if most of your team is low or dead after the take: reset first, even though it costs some of the buff.
basis: pro:Push the side waves before you posture at Baron

when: your team has Baron buff and you hold a lot of unspent gold
asks: do I back with baron
should I recall or push
I've got gold and baron, what do I do
buy first or siege
say: Spend before you siege: recall now and come back with the wave, or stay only if a tower's about to fall.
more: Gold in your pocket does nothing in the fight at their inhibitor. The same gold as an item can decide it.
A recall straight after Baron is the normal play. You return with items while the waves are still building.
Defenders hoping to hold are counting on you showing up with old items and running out of buff.
check: How much gold do you have, and what would it finish?
breaks: Wrong if their team is mostly dead and the base is open: then keep pushing and buy afterward.
basis: pro:A lead is not power until it is spent

when: your team killed Baron while behind in kills and towers
asks: we stole baron, what do we do
we're behind but got baron
how do we use baron from behind
baron comeback, now what
say: Use it to get outer towers and waves back, not to dive; group for one tower, or spread the buff across two lanes safely.
more: Baron does not make you win fights. It makes your minions hard to clear, so use it where no fight is needed.
Every tower you take back closes the gold gap and gives your team room to ward again.
Stop at the point where they can engage on you under their towers. The buff is spent well if you got two towers.
check: Which of their outer towers are still up, and where are their strongest players?
breaks: Wrong if they walk into you one at a time trying to stop it: then take those fights, since you have the numbers.

when: the enemy team killed Baron in the last minute
asks: they got baron, what do we do
how do we defend baron
they have baron buff, do we fight
how do we stop the push
say: Don't fight into the buff; put a wave-clearer in each pushed lane, or group and defend the inhibitor they're hitting hardest.
more: Their plan needs towers. Yours is to lose as few as possible until the buff runs out.
Clear the minions, not the champions. Without the wave they have to dive, and that is your chance.
If they group five in one lane, match it and give up the outer towers elsewhere. An inhibitor matters more.
check: Which lanes are they pushing, and who on your team clears waves fastest?
breaks: Wrong if one of them walks too far forward alone: a quick kill on him ends the siege early.

when: your team killed the Elder Dragon in the last minute
asks: we got elder, what now
how do we use elder
elder buff, do we fight
what do we do with elder dragon
say: Force a fight right now while the buff finishes off low targets, or march on their base if they won't come out.
more: Elder is a fighting buff. It rewards you for starting a fight, where Baron rewards pushing waves.
They know that and will hide under towers. Then you walk the waves in and make them choose between the base and a fight.
Do not recall for long. The buff is running, and every second not spent near them is wasted.
check: How many of you are alive and healthy, and where is the nearest wave?
breaks: Wrong if half your team died taking it: wait for them rather than fighting short-handed, even at the cost of buff time.

when: the enemy team killed the Elder Dragon in the last minute
asks: they got elder, what do we do
do we fight them with elder
how do we survive elder
they have elder buff, now what
say: Don't fight them at all until the buff ends; clear waves from far back, or give a tower rather than get poked low.
more: With Elder, getting low is the same as dying. So the danger is poke, not only a full engage.
Stay far enough back that nothing reaches you, and clear waves with long-range abilities only.
A tower lost is recoverable. A fight lost into Elder at this stage is usually the game.
check: Who on your team clears waves from long range, and which structures can you afford to lose?
breaks: Wrong if they are hitting your nexus towers: then there is nothing left to give and you must fight at your fountain side.

when: one team has taken four dragons
asks: elder's coming, what do we do
how do we set up elder
is elder next
when do we go to elder
say: Elder is the next dragon, so be at the pit early with waves pushed, or pull them to Baron first if you can't hold river.
more: Once a team has soul, the next dragon to spawn is Elder, and whoever takes it usually wins the next fight outright.
The setup is the same as any dragon but matters more: waves first, then vision, then five players together.
If you cannot win the river, starting Baron makes them split or answer, and that can open Elder for you.
check: When does it spawn, where are the mid and bot waves, and is Baron up?
breaks: Wrong if your team is a player down at the spawn: delay with wave clear and poke instead of walking in.

when: between 18:30 and 20:00
asks: baron's about to spawn, what do we do
how do we set up baron
baron soon, where do I go
do we go top side now
say: Baron's up at twenty: push top and mid waves and ward the pit now, or recall first if you're carrying gold.
more: From twenty minutes the top pit holds Baron, and the team with waves pushed there controls who can start it.
Wards placed before the spawn are what let you catch someone walking up, which is the safe way to get it.
A recall now is cheap. A recall after Baron spawns leaves your team four against five at the pit.
check: Where are the top and mid waves, and how much gold are you holding?
breaks: Wrong if a dragon spawns at the same time and matters more, like soul point: set up there instead.

when: all ten players are alive after 20:00
asks: should we start baron
do we just do baron
can we take baron five v five
baron now or wait
say: Start it as bait and turn on whoever walks in, or back off and wait for a pick if they'd win the Smite fight.
more: With everyone alive, finishing Baron is a coin flip on the last hit. Starting it is different: it makes them come to you.
They have to walk through dark jungle to contest. That is when you get the pick, and then you finish it.
If nobody comes and it gets low, take it. If all five arrive healthy, drop it and fight or leave.
check: Is the pit warded for you, where is their jungler, and can your team drop it and turn quickly?
breaks: Wrong if your team is behind or cannot kill it fast: a slow Baron traps you in the pit, so do not start it.
basis: pro:With a lead, Baron is bait before it is a prize

when: an ally is dead and all five enemies are alive after 20:00
asks: they're going to do baron, what do we do
we're four v five, do we contest baron
can we stop baron
do we give baron
say: They may start Baron with you a player down: try the steal only with cover, or trade a tower across the map instead.
more: Four against five in a narrow pit entrance is the worst fight on the map. Walking in usually loses Baron and three more players.
A jungler going for the steal needs teammates close enough to threaten, or he is simply killed on the way.
Pushing a far lane while they hit Baron gets you something. Standing nearby and watching gets you nothing.
check: Can you see them on Baron, how long is your teammate's timer, and which tower can you reach?
breaks: Wrong if the dead ally respawns before they could finish it: then stall and poke until you are five.
basis: pro:If you cannot contest, take something elsewhere at once

when: all five enemies are alive after 20:00
asks: can we sneak baron
should we rush baron
nobody's looking, baron?
quick baron?
say: A sneak works only if they just showed far bot and you kill it fast, or else ward it and wait for a pick.
more: A sneak is a race between your damage and their walk. If they showed on the far side, you have a real head start.
If they are unseen, assume they are close. Being caught low in the pit is how a lead disappears.
The patient version is nearly as good: hold vision, catch one, then take it without the race.
check: Where did the enemies last show, is there an enemy ward on the pit, and how fast does your team kill it?
breaks: Wrong if your team lacks sustained damage or a tank for it: do not start, just keep the area warded.
basis: pro:With a lead, Baron is bait before it is a prize

when: your team won a fight and your health is low
asks: we won but we're all low, baron?
everyone's low, do we take baron
can we do baron on low health
we won the fight, what's safe
say: Low health makes Baron a gift to their respawns; shove one wave and recall, or take a tower if minions tank it.
more: Baron hurts, and it takes time. A low team finishes it even lower, just as the enemy comes back.
A wave and a clean recall keep everything you earned and let you return with items for the real attempt.
A tower is fine when minions take the shots. It costs you no health and cannot be stolen.
check: How low is everyone, how long are their death timers, and is their jungler alive?
breaks: Wrong if four or five of them are dead with long timers: then even a low team can finish Baron safely.
basis: pro:When ahead, let them come to you

when: after 20:00 and a dragon is up
asks: they're on dragon, do we do baron
should we trade baron for dragon
they went bot, baron?
dragon or baron
say: If they're on dragon and you're top side, start Baron and make them choose, or drop it and back off if it's slow.
more: Threatening the second pit moves the fight. They either leave their dragon or let you hit Baron for free.
It only works if your Baron is quick. A slow one gets called as a bluff: they finish dragon and walk up.
Be ready to leave. The goal is to take one objective or pull them, not to be caught low in the pit.
check: Can you see them on dragon, how fast can you kill Baron, and is it their soul dragon?
breaks: Wrong if that dragon gives them soul: Baron is not a fair trade for it, so go and contest instead.
basis: pro:A second objective moves the fight

when: Elder Dragon and Baron are both up
asks: elder or baron
both are up, which one
do we go baron or elder
which objective matters more
say: Elder wins fights outright, so set up there first, or take Baron quickly if they've stacked all five at Elder.
more: If a fight is going to decide the game, the Elder buff decides the fight. That makes it the first priority.
Baron is the answer when they over-commit to the dragon side. It gets you a push while they hold an empty pit.
The team with better wave control can threaten both and make the other guess.
check: How many enemies show at each pit, and which side are your waves pushing toward?
breaks: Wrong if your team cannot fight five on five at all: take Baron and defend with it rather than contest Elder.
basis: pro:A second objective moves the fight

when: your team has three dragons and the next one spawns within a minute
asks: we're on soul point, what do we do
soul dragon's coming, how do we set up
next drake is soul, plan?
how do we get soul
say: This dragon is soul, so recall now and arrive together half a minute early, or threaten Baron to split them if it's up.
more: They have to contest this one, so expect all five. That means you need all five too, with items bought.
Arriving first lets you ward and choose where to stand. Arriving second means walking into their setup.
With soul point in hand there is no rush. If the fight looks bad, you can back off and try again when it suits you.
check: Who needs to recall, where are the mid and bot waves, and is anyone's Teleport up?
breaks: Wrong if someone on your team is dead or far away at the spawn: wait, because the dragon stays there until someone takes it.
basis: pro:Before a spawn, arrive alive and on time

when: the enemy has three dragons and the next one spawns within a minute
asks: they're on soul point, what do we do
do we have to fight this dragon
they're about to get soul
can we give this drake
say: This one you contest: get there first as five with waves pushed, or if you can't, take Baron or towers the moment they start.
more: Earlier dragons can be given. Soul cannot, because it makes every later fight harder for the rest of the game.
Plan recalls and Teleports around this spawn so nobody is in base or in a side lane when it appears.
If the fight is truly unwinnable, be paid in full elsewhere. Do not stand at the river and watch.
check: When does it spawn, is your whole team alive and bought, and is Baron up as a trade?
breaks: Wrong if a teammate is dead at the spawn: stall with poke and wave clear until you are five, and avoid a four against five.
basis: pro:Give early dragons, then fight the one before soul point

when: a dragon was killed in the last 30 seconds
asks: dragon's done, what now
what do we do after drake
where do we go after dragon
next objective?
say: Next dragon is five minutes off, so use the time on top-side towers or Baron, or reset and farm if you're low.
more: A dragon respawns five minutes after it dies, so the bot side goes quiet for a while.
That is the time to recall, buy and move pressure to the other half of the map.
Aim to be back on the dragon side with waves pushed about a minute before the next one.
check: How much gold do you have, and what is up on the top side?
breaks: Wrong if you just lost the fight for it: defend what they push next before thinking about the other side.

when: an objective spawns within a minute and your carry is close to finishing an item
asks: should we recall before dragon
do I buy first or go
I'm almost at my item, do we fight
back or stay for the objective
say: Recall and finish the item before you contest, or give this one if you can't be back in time and it isn't soul.
more: An objective fight on a finished item against components is a different fight. The item is worth the walk.
Recall early enough to be back before the spawn. A recall as it spawns is the worst timing of all.
An early dragon given away is cheap compared with a lost fight that also gives kills and the dragon.
check: How much gold short is the item, and how long until the spawn?
breaks: Wrong if they are the ones about to complete items: then fighting now, before they recall, is your better moment.
basis: pro:Do not fight an objective one spike behind

asks: they're coming, finish or fight
do we finish dragon or turn
they're here, keep hitting it?
burn it or fight
say: Make one call: everyone turns and fights, or everyone burns it down if it's nearly dead. Half and half loses both.
more: A split team has neither the damage to finish the monster nor the bodies to win the fight.
If it is high on health, dropping it is free. It stays there, and you fight at full attention.
If it is nearly dead and your jungler is healthy, finishing first can be right, but everyone has to commit.
check: How much health is left on the objective, and is your jungler alive with Smite?
breaks: Wrong if a bigger objective is up right after: then winning the fight matters more than securing this one.
basis: pro:One call at an objective: finish it or fight

when: between 7:30 and 9:00
asks: grubs are up, do I go
should we fight for grubs
do I leave lane for grubs
are grubs worth it
say: Grubs are one window and don't come back: shove and walk up together, or keep your wave and plates if you'd arrive late.
more: Grubs help you take towers later, so they pay only if your team actually pushes towers afterward.
The cost is whatever you leave behind: a wave, plates, sometimes a tower in the other lane.
Taking some of them and going back to lane is a fine result. It does not have to be all or nothing.
check: Is your wave pushed, who has Teleport, and is their top laner staying in lane?
breaks: Wrong if their mid and jungler are both there first: give it and take plates or the dragon instead.
basis: pro:Price grubs against plates and waves

when: two enemies are dead before 20:00
asks: two dead, what do we take
we got a double, tower or dragon
they're down two, where do we go
five v three, now what
say: Five on three wins any tower: take the one nearest the next dragon, or the dragon itself if it's up.
more: Three defenders cannot hold a tower against five with a wave. This is the cleanest tower you will get.
The tower closest to the next objective is the best one, because it takes away their safe approach.
If the dragon is alive, do that first only when their jungler is among the dead. Otherwise the tower is safer.
check: Is a dragon up, is their jungler dead, and which outer towers still stand?
breaks: Wrong if the kills were far from any wave: without minions the tower is slow, so take camps and a recall instead.

when: two or more allies are dead and all five enemies are alive
asks: we're three v five, what do we do
two of us are dead, do we defend
can we hold this
three of us left, now what
say: Give whatever they're taking; three can't hold it. Clear waves at your inner tower, or recall and buy while you wait.
more: Three against five is not a fight. Every extra death lengthens the time they have to take things.
Fall back one structure further than feels necessary, and clear waves from maximum range.
The game is not lost with an outer tower or a dragon. It is often lost by the third and fourth death.
check: What are they hitting, and how long until your teammates respawn?
breaks: Wrong if they are diving recklessly under a healthy tower with no wave: then punish whoever takes the tower shots.
basis: pro:Arrive together or do not arrive

when: an objective spawns in about a minute and an enemy is alone in a side lane
asks: do we kill him now or wait
there's one alone, do we go
pick before baron?
should we catch the side laner
say: If he can't escape, kill him late enough that he's dead through the spawn, or just take the kill now if he might get away.
more: A numbers edge only matters at the moment of the objective. Killed too early, he is back in time for it.
Late death timers are long, but so is a minute. Compare the two before you commit.
Do not send too many. Two or three for the pick, the rest holding the pit, is the usual split.
check: Does he have Flash or an escape, and how long would his death timer be?
breaks: Wrong if going for him pulls your team away from the pit and his team starts it: hold the objective and ignore him.
basis: pro:Time the pick against the objective clock

when: your team leads in kills but not in towers or dragons
asks: we're ahead in kills, how do we win
we keep getting kills but nothing happens
how do we use this lead
we're winning fights, now what
say: Kills alone fade; group for the next dragon or the weakest outer tower, or shove side waves first so they can't answer both.
more: Kill gold is a lead only until they catch up on farm. Towers and dragons do not go away.
Choose one target and bring the whole team to it after the next kill, instead of five separate chases.
Each outer tower also takes away part of their safe map, and that makes the following objective easier.
check: Which outer towers are lowest, and when does the next dragon spawn?
breaks: Wrong if the kills are all on one teammate who is elsewhere: play around that player's lane rather than forcing without them.
basis: pro:Early dragons are the clock against a scaling team

when: your team is well ahead in kills and towers
asks: should we dive them
can we just run at them
we're way ahead, do we force
do we dive the tower
say: You don't need the dive; hold vision and waves and let them walk into you, or go only with ultimates up on a lone target.
more: When you are far ahead, the safe play is also the strong one. They have to come out, and they come out one at a time.
A greedy dive is the standard way a lead is given back: two deaths, bounties, and a free Baron for them.
Keep the waves pushed and the objectives warded. Their choices get worse every minute you do that.
check: Are your key ultimates up, and is the target really alone?
breaks: Wrong if their team scales much harder than yours and the lead is about to run out: then you do have to force it.
basis: pro:When ahead, let them come to you

when: an enemy inhibitor is down
asks: we got an inhib, what now
inhibitor's down, where do we go
do we keep pushing after inhib
what do we do with super minions
say: Super minions do the pushing there, so move to Baron or the opposite lane, or go as five for a second inhibitor if they're split.
more: That lane now pushes itself, and someone on their team has to stay home to clear it.
So every objective elsewhere is four against five in your favour, or the base takes damage.
Do not stand in the lane with the super minions. Your pressure is worth more wherever they are not.
check: Who stayed to clear the super minions, and is Baron or a dragon up?
breaks: Wrong if your team is low or carrying gold: recall first, because the super minions keep working while you shop.
basis: pro:Push the side waves before you posture at Baron

asks: they're low under tower, do we dive
can we dive them
they're stuck at tower, go in?
should we tower dive
say: Dive only with a full wave tanking and numbers on your side, or keep them pinned and take the objective instead.
more: The tower is their extra player. Minions take its shots for a while, and without them it takes yours.
A team pinned under its tower cannot contest the river. That is often worth more than the kill.
If you do go, wait for the defender's block or escape to be used first, then commit all at once.
check: How many minions are under the tower, who is missing on their team, and is an objective up?
breaks: Wrong if their missing players could arrive mid-dive: then it becomes a lost fight under a tower, so back off.
basis: pro:A dive runs on minions and one defensive button

asks: can I go catch the side wave
should I farm bot
do I go get that wave
wave's pushing, do I leave
say: Catch it only while your team's close or the enemy shows elsewhere, or let it crash and stay with the group.
more: A wave is a little gold. Being caught alone this late can be Baron or the game.
The safe time is when you can count the enemies on the map somewhere else.
If the wave has to be caught, send whoever has an escape or Teleport, not the carry the team fights around.
check: How many enemies can you see on the map, and how far is the wave from your team?
breaks: Wrong if the wave is about to take your inhibitor tower: then someone must go, with the rest hovering close.

asks: they're ending, do we recall
base race?
do we go back or keep pushing
they're in our base, what do we do
say: Race only if you're on their nexus towers with a wave; otherwise recall now, or send your fastest wave-clearer back alone.
more: A base race is decided by who is closer to finishing and who has minions. Guessing wrong loses the game on the spot.
One good wave-clearer at home often stops a small push by killing the minions, while four keep pressure on.
If they have champions and a big wave in your base, everyone goes back. Their structures will still be there.
check: How many of them are in your base, do they have a wave, and how far are you from their nexus?
breaks: Wrong if recall would be interrupted or you'd arrive after it's over: then you are committed, so hit the structure and nothing else.

say: Send your best duelist to the side away from the next objective, or keep five together if nobody can win a one-on-one.

Putting him opposite the objective stretches them the furthest. They cannot be in both places.
If your side laner would lose to whoever they send, the split just gives them a kill, and grouping is better.

more: Each solo death hands them a free objective. Stopping that matters more than any play you could make.
Mid is the easiest place to gather. It is the shortest walk for everyone and covers both rivers.
If they will not group, do not join the next bad fight. Two good players alive can still hold a base.
check: Who is your strongest teammate right now, and where are they?

say: Recall and spend it before the next fight, or stay one more wave only if a tower or objective falls in that time.
more: A gold lead in your pocket is no lead at all. The fight is decided by items already bought.
The best recall is right after a kill or a shoved wave, when nobody can punish you for leaving.
Coming back with an item to the next objective is how one kill turns into two.
check: What does your gold finish, and how long until the next objective?

Teams bunch up at objectives and in jungle paths. Those are the places to look for it.
After it lands, stay on them. Ground Slam slows their attack speed, which blunts their carries while your team follows.

Flame Chompers! at your own feet is your answer to anyone who jumps on you before then.

say: Save Lamb's Respite for when your carry is about to die, or drop it on yourself if you're the main damage.
more: Nothing inside the zone can die while it lasts, and that includes enemies standing in it.
So place it where your team is and theirs is not, or their low players are saved too.
Used late, it buys the seconds your team needs for abilities to come back. Used early, it is wasted.

Time Warp does the rest: speed on a teammate who needs to reach or escape, or a slow on whoever chases.

say: Stand in the middle with Defile on, since dying still lets you cast, or stay back and Requiem if they're low and running.

Wall of Pain across their path slows them and lowers their magic resist before the damage starts.
Requiem hits every enemy champion wherever they are, so it finishes a fight that has scattered.
